review.explanation: 王處仲 is explicitly identified as the courtesy name of 王敦. The candidate evidence from aliases.json directly provides the text where 王處仲 appears, and the Liu annotation (annotation-003) explicitly names 王處仲 in the context of 潘淊's speech about 王敦's bee-like eyes and jackal voice, matching the main text's description of 王敦. The courtesy name 處仲 is a well-established alias for 王敦, and the annotation text corroborates the identity by placing 王處仲 in the same narrative context as the main text's 王敦.

The surface form 王敦 in the main text directly matches the canonical name 王敦. The main text states '潘陽仲見王敦小時' — Pan Yangzhong saw Wang Dun when young. This is a direct name match with no ambiguity. The candidate evidence from people.json confirms 王敦 as a canonical person entry. The low confidence in the reference semantics is due to a failed semantic record, but the name match itself is unambiguous.

The surface form 王敦 in the Liu annotation (annotation-002) directly matches the canonical name 王敦. The annotation text '王夷甫言東海王越轉王敦爲楊州' refers to the same historical figure 王敦 who appears in the main text. The annotation is a commentary on the main text passage about 王敦, and the name match is exact. The annotation also connects to 王處仲 via annotation-003, further confirming this is the same person.

The surface form 君 is a second-person pronoun used by 潘陽仲 (潘淊) addressing 王敦 directly. The main text reads '潘陽仲見王敦小時謂曰君蜂目巳露但豺聲未振耳' — Pan Yangzhong saw Wang Dun when young and said to him 'you have bee eyes already showing...'. The verb 謂 (said to) anchors the speech relation, making 君 the addressee, which is unambiguously 王敦 (the person just mentioned as the object of 見). The pronoun 君 cannot refer to anyone else in this context since the speaker is 潘陽仲 and the only other person in the sentence is 王敦.

The main text states 潘陽仲見王敦小時, explicitly naming 王敦 as the person being observed. The mention surface 敦 is the abbreviated personal name of 王敦. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-07-shijian-006-liu-annotation-003) explicitly glosses 敦 as 王處仲 (Wang Dun's courtesy name), confirming the identity. The annotation also references 王敦 in the context of 潘淊 (太傅), matching the reference semantics that 敦 speaks to the 太傅. The evidence directly supports the identity assertion through explicit naming in the main text and explicit glossing in the annotation.
